activation_signals: The problem asks who / what / which / how many — a unique-attribution or enumeration lookup.
The answer is a proper noun, integer, color name, molecule name, or classification.
The problem stacks multiple constraints that must all be satisfied simultaneously.
The answer depends on a specific classification standard, naming convention, or catalog.
problem_signatures: Humanities: cold-trivia attribution — who wrote / who said / which year / first published.
Chemistry: how many allotropes / colors / isomers / atoms in a named molecule.
Pop culture / brand: which product contains a specific ingredient / which color is named X.
Named molecule trivia: how many carbons/atoms in a fictitious or real named compound.
Extinct-species-named molecules: find the molecule named after a specific extinct taxon.
likely_failure_modes: Using general knowledge consensus instead of the specific authoritative source the question implies.
For chemistry classification questions, applying a more conservative or liberal definition than the source uses.
Drawing a conclusion from a single cue without conjoining all stated constraints.
Giving a near-miss answer on obscure topics.
For multilingual text, failing to translate the key phrase before searching.
subtype_playbook: Named molecule trivia: look up structure in PubChem/ChemSpider or the naming paper.
Allotrope/isomer/polymorph count: enumerate from a specific reference — counts vary by source.
Brand/product color names: consult official product catalog or manufacturer's ingredient list.
Extinct-species-named molecules: search by molecule name pattern + taxon name in chemical databases.
Literary/philosophical attribution: resolve to work → passage → speaker.
Pop culture/game trivia: consult official wiki — never estimate.
